title: Split without leaking the future
concept: Why does a time split need an embargo?
summary: A model that is scored on data recorded before it would have been trained looks better than it is. Splitting chronologically fixes the direction of time, and an embargo period after the cutoff is discarded so that records straddling the boundary cannot carry the answer across it.
example: With a cutoff at 100 and an embargo of 10, records at 95 train, records at 105 are discarded, and records at 110 evaluate.
takeaway: Records inside the embargo are thrown away rather than assigned to either side.
instruction: Given records [{id, at}] and integers cutoff and embargo (nonnegative), return {train, holdout, embargoed} as ID arrays. A record trains when at is below cutoff, is embargoed when at is at least cutoff and below cutoff plus embargo, and is holdout otherwise. Preserve the input order within each list.
hint: Compare each record against two boundaries, cutoff and cutoff plus embargo, and keep the original order.

tests.label: Records on each side of the boundary
A zero embargo keeps every record
The cutoff itself is not training data
Order is preserved within each side
